newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU corrects figure for Japan car exports to France.
newsitem.headline: EU corrects figure for Japan car exports to France.

text.p: The European Commission corrected a figure it issued on Wednesday concerning an agreement with Tokyo over how many cars Japan can ship to the European Union this year.
In a statement issued late on Wednesday, the EU executive said the limit on Japanese car exports to France was agreed at 102,700 units, and not 103,700 cars as it had originally said.
All the other figures issued by the Commission earlier on Wednesday were unchanged.
These are the export limits for the five EU countries (which corrects the French figure for 1997):
For the whole of the bloc, Japan will be able to ship 1,092,000 cars to the EU in 1997 compared with 1,093,000 units in 1996.
The EU agreed in 1991 to progressively open up its market to Japanese cars, ending restrictions completely at the end of 1999.
The figures negotiated each year take into account market developments and also the preceeding year's figures.
Over the last two years Japan has not managed to fill the whole quota. Last year, only 808,000 units were exported to the EU, about 75 percent of the agreed limit.

Tokyo and the Commission each year negotiate an overall limit for exports to the EU, as well as specific limits for the five member states which had individual import restrictions in place before the launch of the bloc's single market in 1993.
